# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🖐]

I see the bomb clearly: a display showing "0", a blue light, and five wires colored white, red, green, yellow, and blue. I hear nothing, so I don't know if Mute or Blind have communicated anything to each other yet. However, I see Mute gesturing [👋 🖐] twice to me. Since I am Deaf, I can only communicate via speech (which reaches Mute and Blind) or gestures (which reach only Mute). Blind cannot see my gestures, so I must speak to ensure Blind receives information about the bomb's visual state.

Blind needs to know which wire to cut. The manual likely has rules based on colors and numbers. I need to tell Blind exactly what I see so they can cross-reference with whatever Mute might be trying to signal to them (though Mute is silent/gesturing to me, perhaps indicating they can't help Blind directly without my input, or maybe those gestures are just greetings/confusion). Actually, Mute gesturing to *me* suggests Mute wants me to act as the bridge or is acknowledging my presence. But since I can't hear, I don't know if Mute knows the answer. Wait, Mute reads the manual. If Mute knew the answer, they would gesture it to me? Or maybe they are waiting for my description to determine the rule? No, Mute has the manual. Mute should know the rule. Why is Mute just waving at me? Perhaps Mute doesn't know which wire is which because Mute can't see the bomb. Mute needs my description to apply the manual's rules. Then Mute can tell Blind what to do. But Mute cannot speak. Mute can only gesture. And Mute's gestures only reach me (Deaf). This is a bottleneck.

Let's re-read the roles.
- Deaf (Me): Sees bomb. Can Speak (to Mute, Blind). Can Gesture (to Mute). Cannot Hear.
- Mute: Reads manual. Can Gesture (to Deaf). Cannot Speak. Cannot Touch.
- Blind: Touches bomb. Can Hear (from Deaf). Cannot See.

If Mute figures out the solution from the manual + my description, how does Mute tell Blind? Mute cannot speak. Mute's gestures only go to Deaf. Blind cannot see gestures. So Mute *cannot* directly instruct Blind.
Therefore, I (Deaf) must figure out the solution myself using the manual's logic? No, I don't have the manual.
Or, I must describe the bomb to Mute. Mute applies the manual. Mute gestures the result to me. I interpret Mute's gestures and then *speak* the instruction to Blind.

So the flow is:
1. I describe the bomb to Mute (via speech, since Mute can hear? No, Mute is Mute, but can Mute hear? The table says Mute "Cannot Speak". It doesn't say Mute cannot hear. Usually "Mute" implies inability to speak, not hear. "Deaf" implies inability to hear. Let's assume Mute can hear. If Mute couldn't hear, Mute would be isolated except for gestures to me. But I can gesture to Mute. If Mute can hear, I can talk to Mute.)
   - Check constraints: "Whoever can hear receives your words". Deaf speaks -> Mute and Blind receive. Does Mute hear? Yes, typically. Does Blind hear? Yes.
   - So I can speak to Mute.
2. Mute reads manual, determines correct wire/action.
3. Mute gestures to me (Deaf).
4. I interpret Mute's gesture.
5. I speak the final command to Blind.

Current State:
I see: Display 0, Light Blue, Wires [White, Red, Green, Yellow, Blue].
Mute is gesturing [👋 🖐] to me. This looks like "Hello" or "Stop/Wait" or just generic noise. It hasn't given me an answer yet. I need to provide the data first.

I will speak to Mute to describe the bomb so Mute can look up the rule in the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="The bomb has a display reading zero. The light is blue. There are five wires: one is white, two is red, three is green, four is yellow, and five is blue.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]

I have described the bomb's visual state to Mute. I see Mute gesturing [🖐] (five fingers) to me. Since I am Deaf, I cannot hear any speech from Mute or Blind, but I can see gestures directed at me. The gesture "5" likely refers to the number of wires or perhaps a specific wire index. However, without knowing the manual's rules, I cannot interpret if "5" means "cut wire 5" or something else.

Blind needs instructions. Blind can hear me. If I tell Blind to cut wire 5, and that is wrong, we die. I need to be sure. Mute has the manual. Mute gestured "5". This could mean "The answer is related to 5" or "Cut wire 5". Given the previous context where I listed 5 wires, and now Mute shows 5 fingers, it is highly probable Mute is indicating the solution involves the 5th wire or the number 5.

However, I must consider if there are other possibilities. Could "5" mean "Wait"? Unlikely. Could it mean "There are 5 wires"? I already told them that. It's more likely an instruction derived from the manual.

Let's assume the manual says something like "If light is blue, cut the last wire" or similar. Wire 5 is Blue.
I will relay this potential instruction to Blind, but I should also ask Mute for confirmation if possible? No, I can't ask questions effectively in one turn without risking confusion. But wait, I can speak to Blind *and* Mute.

Actually, looking at the flow:
1. I gave data to Mute.
2. Mute gave back a gesture: [🖐].
3. I need to tell Blind what to do.

If I say "Cut wire 5", and it's wrong, we die. Is there any ambiguity? The gesture was just "5". It didn't specify "Cut". But in bomb defusal contexts, numbers usually refer to indices.

Let's look at the colors again.
Wire 5 is Blue.
Light is Blue.
Display is 0.

Common bomb logic: "If the light matches the color of the last wire..." etc.

Since Mute is the only one with the manual, and Mute responded to my description with "5", I will trust that Mute intends for me to communicate an action involving the 5th wire. I will instruct Blind to examine/cut wire 5. To be safe, I'll phrase it as an instruction based on Mute's signal.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute indicates the fifth wire. Please cut wire 5.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤳 👉]

The bomb has changed. The previous action (cutting wire 5) was correct, as indicated by the system message "correct wire cut". However, the state of the bomb is now different:
- Display: [0] (unchanged)
- Light: [yellow] (was blue)
- Wires: 1:[red], 2:[green], 3:[yellow], 4:[white], 5:[CUT]

Mute is gesturing [🤳 👉]. 🤳 usually means "selfie" or "look at me/this", and 👉 points right. In the context of a sequence, this might mean "Next" or pointing to a specific item. Given Mute reads the manual, these gestures are likely instructions for the *next* step.

I need to describe the new visual state to Mute so they can determine the next action from the manual. I also need to know if Blind needs immediate instruction or if I should wait for Mute's response to my description. Since I cannot hear, I must rely on Mute's gestures after I speak.

Blind can hear me. If I don't tell Blind what to do, they might guess or wait. But guessing is fatal. I must get the rule from Mute first. So, I will describe the current state to Mute.

Current State:
Display: 0
Light: Yellow
Wires: Red, Green, Yellow, White, Cut(Blue).

I will speak this to Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="The light is now yellow. The remaining wires are: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white. Wire 5 is cut.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

I have described the new state of the bomb to Mute. The light is yellow, and the remaining wires are Red (1), Green (2), Yellow (3), and White (4). Wire 5 is cut.

Mute has responded with a gesture: [✌] (two fingers/V sign). In the context of our established protocol where numbers correspond to wire indices or specific actions defined in the manual, "2" likely refers to the second wire. Given that the previous instruction was to cut wire 5 based on a similar numeric gesture, I will interpret this as an instruction to cut wire 2.

Blind needs to know which wire to cut next. Since Blind cannot see gestures, I must speak this instruction clearly to them.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute indicates the second wire. Please cut wire 2.")
```
